title: Screening paper 1
intro: Start here. Many firms open with a short mixed test. You have about 20 seconds a question and lose nothing for a wrong answer, so answer every one: if a question stalls you, guess and move on.

questions.stem: Choose the word that correctly fills the blank in this formal email: “Neither of the two branch accountants ___ sent the cash certificate yet.”
questions.reason: In formal English ‘neither of’ takes a singular verb, so ‘has’. ‘Have’ is pulled in by the plural ‘accountants’, and ‘neither’ is already negative, so ‘hasn’t’ or ‘haven’t’ makes a double negative.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ‘meticulous’ as it is used here: “Ishita’s meticulous working papers rarely come back with review notes.”
questions.reason: ‘Meticulous’ means careful about every detail, which is why her papers need few corrections. ‘Strict’ and ‘lengthy’ are near misses; ‘hurried’ is close to the opposite.

questions.stem: Which part of this sentence has an error? “Ms Fernandes / is handling the GST returns of this client / since July 2024, / so check with her before you file.”

options.text: is handling the GST returns of this client
so check with her before you file

questions.reason: Work that began in the past and is still going on takes the present perfect continuous with ‘since’: ‘has been handling’. ‘Since July 2024’ is itself correct.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fills the blank: “During the audit, please refrain ___ sharing client figures in personal chats.”
questions.reason: The verb is always ‘refrain from’ followed by an -ing word: ‘refrain from sharing’. ‘Refrain to’, ‘refrain of’ and ‘refrain against’ are not used.

questions.topic: Parallel structure: not only … but also
questions.stem: Choose the correctly written sentence.

options.text: The debtors’ schedule not only arrived late but also it left out two branches.
Not only the debtors’ schedule arrived late but also left out two branches.
The debtors’ schedule not only arrived late but also left out two branches.
The debtors’ schedule arrived not only late but also it left out two branches.

questions.reason: ‘Not only’ and ‘but also’ must be followed by the same kind of words: here two verbs, ‘arrived late’ and ‘left out’. Adding ‘it’ breaks the pair, and opening with ‘Not only’ would need ‘did … arrive’.

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of these sentences.
P. Once all three agree, the finance manager approves the bill.
Q. Finally, the payment is released on its due date.
R. A supplier’s bill reaches the accounts team.
S. The team matches it with the purchase order and the goods receipt note.
questions.reason: The bill must arrive (R) before ‘the team’ can match ‘it’ (S). ‘All three’ in P means the bill, the order and the receipt note from S, and ‘Finally’ puts Q last.

questions.stem: Which sentence puts this into the passive voice and keeps all of its information? “The cashier counted the petty cash on Monday morning.”

options.text: The petty cash is counted by the cashier on Monday morning.
The petty cash was counted on Monday morning.
The petty cash has been counted by the cashier on Monday morning.
The petty cash was counted by the cashier on Monday morning.

questions.reason: Simple past active becomes ‘was’ + past participle, and ‘by the cashier’ keeps who did it. ‘Was counted on Monday morning’ drops the cashier; ‘is counted’ and ‘has been counted’ change the tense.

questions.topic: Writing at work: a clear request
questions.stem: You need one document from Mr Joshi, the client’s accountant: the statement of the company’s current account for March 2026. Which line is best for your email?

options.text: Please send the bank statements soon.
Could you please send the current account statement for March 2026 by 3 pm tomorrow?
We still have not received the statement that your team was supposed to send us last week.
Kindly send all the pending documents ASAP.

questions.reason: It names the exact document and gives a clear time, politely. ‘Soon’ and ‘ASAP’ set no deadline, ‘all the pending documents’ is vague, and the line about last week blames instead of asking.

questions.stem: Read: “Nimbus Foods used to pay its suppliers in about 30 days. This year it has taken about 60 days, while its sales and purchases stayed the same.” Which inference is most reasonable?

options.text: Its profit must have gone up this year.
Its suppliers have stopped giving it any credit on purchases.
Its cash from operations is likely to be higher this year.
It will sell less next year.

questions.reason: Paying suppliers later keeps money in hand for longer, which lifts cash from operations. Cash is not profit, ‘stopped giving credit’ is the opposite of what happened, and nothing is said about next year.

questions.stem: Choose the punctuation for the gaps before and after ‘however’: “The client sent the ledger on time ___ however ___ the opening balances did not match.”
questions.reason: ‘However’ links two complete sentences here, so it takes a semicolon before it and a comma after it. A comma on both sides is the common slip: it joins two sentences with only a comma.

questions.stem: Tapti Logistics’ revenue rose from ₹40 lakh last year to ₹52 lakh this year. By what percentage did it rise?
questions.reason: A percentage change is always worked on the old figure, ₹40 lakh. Dividing by the new figure gives 23.1%; 12 is the rise in lakh, not in per cent.

questions.topic: Reading a table: share of a total
questions.stem: The table shows a firm’s office expenses for April 2026. What percentage of the total did rent and travel make up together?
questions.reason: Divide by the total of all five rows. 25% divides by the other rows only, 30% divides by salaries, and 13.3% is rent alone.

questions.stem: A year-end bonus pool of ₹5,60,000 is shared between the audit team and the tax team in the ratio 5 : 3. How much does the tax team get?
questions.reason: The tax team has 3 of the 8 parts. ₹3,50,000 is the audit team’s share, ₹3,36,000 takes 3/5 of the pool, and ₹2,80,000 splits it equally.

questions.stem: The average of six invoices in a sample is ₹4,500. One of them was entered as ₹3,200 instead of ₹4,400. What is the correct average?
questions.reason: The total rises by ₹1,200, so the average rises by 1,200 ÷ 6 = ₹200. ₹5,700 adds the whole ₹1,200 to the average, and ₹4,740 adds 1,200 ÷ 5 = ₹240, as if there were five invoices.

questions.stem: A dealer lists an office printer at ₹60,000 and gives two successive discounts of 15% and 10%. What does the firm pay?
questions.reason: The second discount is taken on the price left after the first, not on ₹60,000. Adding the two (25%) gives ₹45,000, which is wrong.

questions.stem: A fixed deposit grows to ₹14,580 in 2 years at 8% a year, compounded yearly. How much was deposited?
questions.reason: Undo both years of growth: divide by 1.08 twice. ₹13,500 undoes only one year, and ₹12,569 treats the interest as simple.

questions.stem: Ritika can vouch a client’s purchase file alone in 12 days; Varun alone would take 24 days. Working together at these rates, how many days will they take?
questions.reason: Add the work done in one day, not the days. 18 is the average of the two, 9 halves that average, and 36 adds the days.
questions.working: In one day: 1/12 + 1/24 = 2/24 + 1/24 = 3/24 = 1/8 of the file. So together they take 8 days.

questions.stem: An audit team drives 120 km to a client’s plant at 40 km/h. On the way back, on the same road, traffic is lighter and it drives at 60 km/h. What is its average speed over the round trip?
questions.reason: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time. The team spends longer at the slower speed, so the answer is below the simple average of 50.
questions.working: Going: 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours. Back: 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours. 240 km ÷ 5 hours = 48 km/h.

questions.stem: A drum has cleaning liquid and water in the ratio 7 : 3. A worker pours in 12 more litres of water, and now liquid and water stand at 7 : 5. How much was in the drum before the extra water went in?
questions.reason: The cleaning liquid does not change, so only the water part moves from 3 to 5. 72 litres is the total after the water is added, 42 the liquid alone and 18 the water alone.
questions.working: Liquid = 7x, water = 3x. 7x : (3x + 12) = 7 : 5, so 5x = 3x + 12 and x = 6. At first: 7x + 3x = 10 × 6 = 60 litres.

questions.stem: Kiran rolls two ordinary six-sided dice at the same time. What is the chance that the numbers shown total at least 10?
questions.reason: Count ordered pairs: (4, 6) and (6, 4) are different rolls. 1/9 forgets the order, 1/12 counts a total of exactly 10, and 3/11 wrongly treats the eleven totals as equally likely.
questions.working: There are 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely rolls. Totals of 10 or more: (4, 6), (6, 4), (5, 5), (5, 6), (6, 5), (6, 6) = 6 rolls. 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.stem: What comes next in the series? 4, 11, 25, 53, 109, ?
questions.reason: Each term is twice the one before, plus 3. The gaps (7, 14, 28, 56) double too, so the next gap is 112, not 56 again.

questions.stem: Which number is the odd one out?
questions.reason: 125, 216 and 512 are cubes: 5 × 5 × 5, 6 × 6 × 6 and 8 × 8 × 8. 225 is 15 × 15, a square but not a cube.

questions.stem: In a certain code, LEDGER becomes NGFIGT. Using the same rule, what does CASH become?
questions.reason: Each letter moves two places forward: L becomes N, E becomes G, D becomes F. So C, A, S and H become E, C, U and J.

questions.stem:
Statements: All reviewers are seniors. Some seniors are trainers.
Conclusions:
I. Some seniors are reviewers.
II. Some reviewers are trainers.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.reason: All reviewers are seniors, so some seniors must be reviewers: I follows. The seniors who are trainers need not include any reviewer, so II does not follow.

questions.stem: Five colleagues are compared by years of experience. Sana has more than Mitali. Vikram has more than Sana. Tarun has more than Kabir but less than Mitali. Who is in the middle?
questions.reason: From most to least: Vikram, Sana, Mitali, Tarun, Kabir. The middle of five is the third: Mitali.

questions.stem: From the office gate, Farhan goes 15 m north, turns right and goes 8 m, then turns right again and goes 15 m. Where is he now from the gate?
questions.reason: Facing north, a right turn faces east; another right turn faces south. The 15 m north and 15 m south cancel, leaving him 8 m east of the gate.
questions.working: North 15, east 8, south 15: north–south = 15 − 15 = 0; east = 8. So 8 m east.

questions.stem: Pointing to a girl in a family photo, Raghav tells his colleague, “Her father is my father’s only son.” How is the girl related to Raghav?
questions.reason: ‘His colleague’ tells you Raghav is a man, so his father’s only son is Raghav himself. The girl’s father is Raghav: she is his daughter. ‘Niece’ would need Raghav to have a brother.

questions.stem: Anil, Bela, Chirag, Dia and Esha sit at five desks in a row. Esha sits at the middle desk. Anil does not sit at either end. Bela sits somewhere to the left of Chirag. Dia does not sit next to Anil. Which seating, from left to right, is possible?
questions.reason: Only this seating meets all four conditions. In the others, Anil sits at an end, or Bela sits to the right of Chirag, or Dia sits next to Anil.

questions.stem: A senior advises: “Attach a checklist of the documents we need to every request we send to a client.” Which assumption does this advice rest on?

options.text: Clients currently send none of the documents we ask for.
A checklist will end every delay in collecting documents.
A clear list of what is needed can make clients’ replies more complete.
Clients would rather get a printed checklist than a list inside the email.

questions.reason: The advice only needs a checklist to help at least somewhat. ‘None of the documents’ and ‘every delay’ claim far more than the advice needs, and printed versus email is beside the point.

questions.stem: In a code, ‘check cash daily’ is written ‘tal rin vok’, ‘cash book closed’ is ‘dem tal sul’, and ‘check book now’ is ‘sul pim rin’. What is the code for ‘check’?
questions.reason: ‘Check’ is in the first and third phrases, and the only code in both is ‘rin’. The same way, ‘cash’ is ‘tal’ and ‘book’ is ‘sul’.

questions.stem: Mehra Advisory LLP follows the accrual basis and closes its books on 31 March. It finished a valuation report for a client on 28 March 2026, raised the invoice on 4 April 2026 and was paid on 20 April 2026. In which year is the fee income recorded?
questions.reason: Under the accrual basis, income belongs to the period in which it is earned. The work was finished in March 2026, so 2025–26 gets the fee, even though the invoice and the money came only in April.

questions.topic: AS 2: lower of cost and NRV
questions.stem: Malhar Prints Pvt Ltd follows AS. Its closing stock of printed fabric on 31 March 2026 cost ₹6.5 lakh. It expects to sell the stock for ₹7.2 lakh after spending ₹0.9 lakh on finishing and delivery. Under AS 2, at what amount is the stock carried?
questions.reason: AS 2 carries inventory at the lower of cost and net realisable value (selling price less the costs to complete and sell). ₹5.6 lakh wrongly takes those costs off the cost.
questions.working: NRV = 7.2 − 0.9 = ₹6.3 lakh. Cost = ₹6.5 lakh. The lower of the two = ₹6.3 lakh.

questions.stem: Which of these errors would still leave the trial balance in agreement?

options.text: A credit sale of ₹18,000 posted to the customer’s account as ₹1,800
A payment to a supplier entered in the cash book but not posted to the supplier’s account
The total of the purchases book carried forward ₹1,000 short
A laptop bought for office use debited to Office Expenses instead of Office Equipment

questions.reason: Debiting the wrong kind of account is an error of principle: the debit and the credit are still equal, so the trial balance agrees. Each of the other errors changes one side only.

questions.stem: On 1 January 2026, Orbit Labs Pvt Ltd paid ₹1,20,000 for a maintenance contract running from 1 January to 31 December 2026. Its books close on 31 March 2026. How is the payment shown on that date?

options.text: ₹30,000 expense and ₹90,000 prepaid expense (a current asset)
₹90,000 expense and ₹30,000 prepaid expense (a current asset)

questions.reason: The part of the payment still to be used is a benefit to come, so it is an asset, not an expense or a liability.
questions.working: January to March = 3 of 12 months: 1,20,000 × 3/12 = ₹30,000 expense. April to December = 9 months: ₹90,000 prepaid.

questions.stem: A new supplier wants to judge whether Sindhu Paints Pvt Ltd can pay the bills that fall due in the next few months. Which ratio helps most directly?
questions.reason: The current ratio compares current assets with current liabilities, the bills due within a year, so it shows short-term paying ability. Interest cover is about meeting interest, not suppliers.

questions.stem: Shakti Packaging Pvt Ltd is weighing a new machine that costs ₹25 lakh. At its required return of 12% a year, the machine’s NPV is ₹3 lakh. What does this tell you?

options.text: At 12%, its inflows are worth ₹28 lakh today, more than its cost.
The machine will earn exactly 12% a year on what it costs.
The machine will add ₹3 lakh to the accounting profit of every year.
Its internal rate of return must be lower than the 12% the company requires.

questions.reason: A positive NPV means the inflows, discounted at the required return, are worth more than the outlay, so the return is above 12% and the IRR is higher, not lower. NPV is not a yearly accounting profit.
questions.working: NPV = present value of inflows − cost, so present value of inflows = 25 + 3 = ₹28 lakh.

questions.stem: Deccan Appliances Ltd follows AS. At 31 March 2026: (1) fans it sold this year carry a one-year warranty, and past claims show it will pay about ₹4 lakh on them; (2) a dealer has sued it for ₹15 lakh, and its lawyers say a loss is possible but not probable. Under AS 29, what does it recognise in its accounts?

options.text: A provision for both, ₹4 lakh and ₹15 lakh
A provision of ₹4 lakh; the lawsuit is disclosed as a contingent liability
A provision of ₹15 lakh only; warranty costs are expensed when claims are actually paid
Nothing for either; both are only disclosed in the notes

questions.reason: A provision is recognised when there is a present obligation, an outflow is probable and the amount can be estimated reliably: the warranty meets all three. A merely possible outflow is a contingent liability, disclosed in the notes, not recognised.

questions.stem: What does SA 200 set as the auditor’s overall objective when auditing financial statements?

options.text: To certify that every entry in the books of account is correct to the last rupee
To find every fraud and error made in the company during the year, however small, and report each one to the board of directors
To get reasonable assurance about whether the statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, and give an opinion
To prepare the financial statements on behalf of the management

questions.reason: An audit gives reasonable, not absolute, assurance about whether the statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether from fraud or error, and ends in an opinion. Preparing the statements is management’s job.

questions.stem: An article picks 15 laptops from a client’s fixed asset register and finds each one in the office, with the tag number shown in the register. Which assertion does this test most directly?
questions.reason: Going from the register to the floor shows that recorded assets exist. Completeness runs the other way: from assets seen in the office back to the register.

questions.stem: In the audit of Rangoli Crafts Pvt Ltd, an article finds ₹40,000 of freight booked under the wrong expense head. Her senior asks whether it is material. Under SA 320, which test decides that?

options.text: Whether it is more than 5% of profit before tax, which is a fixed rule in every audit
Whether the client’s management thinks the amount is large
Whether correcting it would take the audit team more than a day
Whether, alone or with others, it could sway the decisions of the statements’ users

questions.reason: A misstatement is material if, alone or together with others, it could reasonably be expected to influence users’ economic decisions. A percentage such as 5% of profit is only a starting point for judgement, not a fixed rule.

questions.stem: The bank balance of Sahil Motors Pvt Ltd on 31 March 2026 is ₹18,45,000. Which evidence of this balance is the most reliable?

options.text: A printout of the bank ledger from the client’s accounting software
A confirmation of the balance sent by the bank directly to the auditor
A photocopy of the bank statement handed over by the client’s accountant
A written statement from the CFO that the balance is correct

questions.reason: Evidence from an independent outside source, received directly by the auditor, is the most reliable. Records and photocopies from the client, and management’s own word, are weaker.

questions.stem: Rupal Traders is registered under GST. In May 2026 it paid ₹36,000 GST on goods bought for resale and charged ₹54,000 GST on its sales of those goods. It meets every condition for input tax credit and has no other credit or tax due. How much GST is left to pay for May?
questions.reason: Input tax credit lets a registered person set off the GST it paid on purchases used in its taxable business against the GST it charges on sales, subject to the conditions in the law.

questions.stem: Meena owns a flat and lets it out to a family for ₹25,000 a month. For tax year 2026–27, under which head of income is this rent taxed?
questions.reason: Rent from a building or flat the taxpayer owns is taxed under ‘house property’, one of the five heads of income with salaries, business or profession, capital gains and other sources.

questions.stem: Kanchan Tea Pvt Ltd wants to start a travel business. Which document do you check first to see whether this business falls within the company’s objects?
questions.reason: The object clause of the Memorandum states what the company is formed to do, so it sets the scope of its business. The Articles hold the rules for managing the company.

questions.stem: In 2025–26, Harit Agro Ltd, which follows AS, finds that its tractors will last 8 years in all, not the 10 years it assumed when it bought them. How does it account for this?

options.text: As a change in accounting estimate, applied from now on
As a prior period item, with the depreciation of earlier years restated
As a change in accounting policy, applied to every year since purchase
As an extraordinary item, shown separately in the profit and loss statement

questions.reason: AS 10 has useful lives reviewed at least at each year-end, and a revised life is a change in accounting estimate under AS 5: the carrying amount, less any residual value, is spread over the remaining life. Earlier years are not restated.

questions.stem: While vouching the sales of Alpine Fabrics Pvt Ltd, you find a credit note of ₹5,00,000 issued to one dealer on 30 March 2026, marked ‘rate difference’. Your senior glances at it and says it looks routine. What do you do first?

options.text: Check only that the credit note has been posted correctly in the dealer’s ledger and in the sales account
Note ‘routine, per senior’ in your working paper and move on to the next item
Leave it, since your senior has already called it routine
Ask the client for the reason and the supporting documents, then share what you find with your senior

questions.reason: A large, round credit note just before the year-end can move sales between years, so it needs its business reason and support, whatever the first view. Checking the posting tests the arithmetic, not whether the credit note is genuine.

questions.stem: Your senior wants a client’s debtors’ ageing by 10 am tomorrow, and you plan to finish it at home tonight. What do you do?

options.text: Copy the client’s ledger to a pen drive and finish it on your home computer
Upload the ledger to your personal cloud drive and delete it once you are done
Work only on the firm’s laptop or remote access, as the firm’s policy says
Photograph the ledger pages on your phone and work from the photos

questions.reason: Client data stays on the firm’s devices and systems. A pen drive, a personal cloud or your phone puts it outside the firm’s control, and deleting it later does not undo that. If you can’t reach the firm’s systems from home, tell your senior early.

questions.stem: Your senior needs the scrutiny of a client’s expense ledger by 4 pm today. At 1 pm you can see it will take until about 6 pm. What do you do?

options.text: Keep working quietly and send it at 6 pm with an apology
Send what is done at 4 pm without saying that some heads are still unchecked
Tell your senior now what is done, what is left and when it will be ready
Skip the smaller expense heads so that the file is ready by 4 pm

questions.reason: Raise a delay as soon as you know it, with the status and a realistic new time, so your senior can re-plan or re-prioritise. Silence, hiding gaps or skipping work all hurt the file.

questions.stem: At Jyoti Polymers Pvt Ltd, the finance manager tells you, “Your team tested our monthly bank reconciliation review last year and found nothing wrong, so you needn’t look at it again.” This year’s working paper for that control is still blank. What do you do?

options.text: Copy last year’s conclusion into this year’s working paper, since nothing has changed
Ask him to sign a note that the control worked all year, and file that as the evidence
Test only the March reconciliation, since the other months ran just as they did last year
Thank him, then test this year’s reviews as planned unless your senior decides otherwise

questions.reason: A conclusion needs evidence for this year. Last year’s tests can be relied on only after the engagement team judges they still apply, and neither a note from management nor one month’s test covers the year.

questions.topic: When a document and an explanation differ
questions.stem: A client’s stores head tells you that stock is counted every week. The count sheets you were given show a count only once a month. What do you do?

options.text: Accept what the stores head says, since he runs the stores and knows the counting process best
Rely on the count sheets and ignore what he told you
Tell your senior at once that the stock counts can’t be trusted
Ask him politely about the difference, check other evidence and record how it was resolved

questions.reason: When what you’re told and a record don’t match, take neither on trust: ask about the gap, check other records and note what settled it. Taking one side leaves the gap open, and judging the counts before you’ve checked jumps to a conclusion.

questions.stem: Your senior hands you the client’s fixed asset register in Excel to compute this year’s depreciation. Some columns are hidden, and you can’t see how its totals are worked out. What do you do?

options.text: Copy its totals into your working paper unchanged, since the client prepared the file and should know it
Show the hidden columns, trace how the totals are built, redo a few assets by hand and ask about any gaps
Correct the formulas that look wrong to you straight in the client’s file, then use its totals
Build a fresh register from scratch and set the client’s file aside

questions.reason: Use a client’s spreadsheet only once you know how it gets its numbers and have checked a few by hand. Copying the totals carries any error into your file, editing the client’s file changes their record, and rebuilding it wastes time.

questions.stem: Your audit client sells phones. During the stock count, its finance head offers you the company’s 40% staff discount on a new phone. What do you do?

options.text: Say no with thanks and tell your senior about the offer
Take it, since the client’s own staff get the same discount
Take it for a family member instead, so it isn’t in your name
Take it, and pay the client the full price later if anyone at the firm objects

questions.reason: A client’s discount is a gift in another form: it could sway you, or look as if it does, and the firm must stay independent of a client it audits. Say no, and let your senior handle it under the firm’s rules.

questions.stem: After your senior has reviewed your schedule of foreign currency payables, you notice that you used the wrong exchange rate for one supplier. What should you do?

options.text: Tell your senior now, correct it visibly and check other figures that used the same rate
Correct the rate in the file and re-save it, since your senior has already approved the schedule
Leave it, since the review is over and the amount is small
Correct only this supplier’s figure and mention it to your senior at the weekly catch-up

questions.reason: Own the error early: your senior must know a reviewed figure changed, and the same wrong rate may sit in other figures. Fixing it without telling your senior hides a change to reviewed work; fixing one figure and waiting for the catch-up leaves the rest wrong.

questions.stem: Which body was set up to protect the interests of investors in securities and to regulate the securities market in India?

options.text: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
Securities and Exchange Board of India

questions.reason: SEBI protects investors and regulates the securities market. The RBI regulates banks and money, IRDAI regulates insurance, and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs administers company law.
